Setting u=t*x^(n-2),v=x^n in H=H'=0 and eliminating v gives only the singular branch u=-n/2 and the smooth jump u=n(n-1)(n-3)/2, v=(n-2)(n-3)^2/2; gcd(n,n-2)=g yields exactly g repeated finite roots and H'' nonzero yields double roots. The simple/double Hessian intersection multiplicities give contact-three/four over each of n y-roots; local expansions at x=0 and y=0 give contact n-2 and n, respectively. Fermat and Hessian total weight 3n(n-2) check boundaries. Independent finite SymPy checks are corroboration, not the proof for every n.
